# Feature Specification: Friday-Night Foundation

**Feature Branch**: `main` (solo hackathon; no feature branch)

**Created**: 2026-11-20

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "Friday-night foundation for Mustang City, per docs/product-brief.md. Installable iPhone PWA shell with phone frame on laptops; full-screen sunset-styled 3D map of London (Forest State) with branded loading; 2D/45° city view easing to detailed 3D over Western campus (Mustang City); first pass of the black fog with local/demo reveal; @uwo.ca-only login; database schema and seed with verified landmark missions; app shell with top HUD and bottom tab bar. Degrade gracefully when configuration is missing. Out of scope: photo verification, friends, replay, extended features."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Open the app and see Forest State under fog (Priority: P1)

A Western student adds Mustang City to their iPhone home screen and opens it. A branded loading
screen shows until the map is fully drawn, then a full-screen, tilted, sunset-lit map of London
appears. Every area they haven't explored is covered in black fog; a cleared patch around
their location (or a demo starting area) shows the city beneath. A top HUD shows Rep, rank and
% explored; a bottom tab bar offers Map, Missions, Crew and Profile.

**Why this priority**: This is the product's one image ("black fog clearing as you walk") and
the first thing judges see. Everything else builds on it.

**Independent Test**: Open the deployed URL on an iPhone home-screen icon and on a laptop;
confirm the loader, the fogged 3D sunset map, the HUD and the tab bar appear, and that a demo
reveal clears fog and raises % explored.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the app is opened from the home-screen icon, **When** it launches, **Then** it fills
   the screen edge to edge (no browser chrome), with HUD and tab bar clear of the notch and home bar.
2. **Given** the app is opened on a laptop browser wider than 768 px, **When** it loads, **Then** the
   identical phone layout is shown in a centered phone-shaped frame on a sunset backdrop.
3. **Given** the map is still loading, **When** the user waits, **Then** only the branded loading
   screen is visible — never a half-drawn map.
4. **Given** the map has loaded, **When** the user looks at it, **Then** it is tilted (~45°), uses
   the sunset palette with lighting matching London's current time of day, shows a horizon glow,
   shows no point-of-interest or transit clutter, and has no default map controls.
5. **Given** the user has explored nothing, **When** the map loads, **Then** all of London is
   covered in solid black fog except the revealed area, with soft edges.
6. **Given** location permission is granted (or the demo reveal is triggered), **When** a new
   position is received, **Then** fog clears around it and % explored in the HUD increases.

---

### User Story 2 - Zoom into Mustang City in 3D (Priority: P1)

From the city view the student zooms toward Western's campus. Once close enough over campus,
the camera smoothly tilts further into a detailed 3D view where campus buildings are highlighted
and mission buildings (e.g. Middlesex College) glow. Zooming back out eases back to the city view.

**Why this priority**: The brief names this the main wow moment of the demo and says to build
it first.

**Independent Test**: On the deployed app, pinch/scroll into campus and back out; confirm the
eased tilt change, highlighted buildings, and return to the city view, with no jumps.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the city view, **When** the user zooms past street level inside the campus area,
   **Then** the camera eases to ~60° pitch and campus buildings appear highlighted in 3D.
2. **Given** the campus 3D view, **When** the user zooms out or pans away from campus, **Then** the
   camera eases back to the ~45° city pitch.
3. **Given** any camera change, **When** it happens, **Then** it is animated (no instant jump).

---

### User Story 3 - Sign in with a Western account (Priority: P2)

The student taps Profile and signs in. Only @uwo.ca accounts are accepted; anyone else is
refused with a clear message. Once signed in, the profile tab shows their name and email, and
they can sign out.

**Why this priority**: Required for profiles, friends and missions tomorrow, and for the Auth0
track, but the map demo works without it.

**Independent Test**: Sign in with a @uwo.ca account from the home-screen app and see the profile;
attempt a non-@uwo.ca account and see it refused.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a signed-out user, **When** they tap Sign in and use a @uwo.ca account, **Then** they
   return to the app signed in and the Profile tab shows their identity.
2. **Given** a non-@uwo.ca account, **When** they try to sign in, **Then** access is denied with an
   explanation that only Western accounts are allowed.
3. **Given** a signed-in user, **When** they sign out, **Then** they return to the signed-out state.
4. **Given** login is not configured in an environment, **When** the user opens Profile, **Then** the
   app shows a "sign-in unavailable" state and the map keeps working.

---

### User Story 4 - Game data foundation (Priority: P2)

The builder can create the full game database (users, location history, revealed areas,
neighbourhoods, missions, completions, heists, friendships, crews, tags, collectibles, badges,
votes, rides, district control) with one command and seed it with the verified landmark missions,
starter missions and badges, so missions and progression can be built tomorrow.

**Why this priority**: Unblocks Saturday's mission and progression work; not visible in tonight's demo.

**Independent Test**: Run the schema and seed commands against an empty database; confirm all
tables exist, location history is time-partitioned, per-user explored counts can be queried, and
the seeded missions and badges are present. Re-running the seed does not duplicate rows.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an empty database, **When** the schema command runs, **Then** every table in the brief's
   data model exists with its keys and constraints.
2. **Given** the schema exists, **When** the seed runs twice, **Then** the 6 verified landmark
   missions, 10–15 starter missions and 6 starter badges exist exactly once.

---

### Edge Cases

- Location permission denied or unavailable (laptop, indoors): the map still loads; fog shows the
  default campus reveal; demo controls can reveal areas.
- Location fixes with poor accuracy (> ~50 m) or implying impossible speed are ignored.
- Map token missing: the app shows a branded "map unavailable" state instead of crashing.
- Slow network: the loader stays until the map is ready; a long wait shows a retry hint.
- Laptop window resized: the phone frame rescales and the map redraws to fit without distortion.
- User has reduced-motion enabled: camera and UI transitions are shortened.
- Position outside London: no fog is cleared (only cells inside the city count).

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: App MUST be installable to the iPhone home screen and launch full screen in portrait
  with the sunset theme and a branded icon.
- **FR-002**: On screens wider than 768 px the app MUST render the same layout inside a centered
  phone frame (~430×932 aspect), scaled to fit the window height.
- **FR-003**: App MUST show a branded loading screen until the map has finished its first full draw.
- **FR-004**: The map MUST show London in 3D at ~45° pitch with the sunset palette, horizon glow,
  lighting by London local time (day / dusk / night), and with POI labels, transit labels and
  default controls hidden. District names remain visible.
- **FR-005**: When zoomed past street level within the Western campus area, the camera MUST ease
  to ~60° pitch with campus buildings highlighted and mission buildings emphasised; leaving that
  zoom or area MUST ease back to ~45°.
- **FR-006**: All camera changes MUST be animated.
- **FR-007**: Unexplored parts of London MUST be covered in solid black fog; explored areas
  (~65 m hex cells) MUST be clear with a soft edge.
- **FR-008**: While the app is open and permission is granted, each accepted location fix MUST
  reveal the current cell and its immediate neighbours; fixes worse than ~50 m accuracy or
  implying impossible speed MUST be ignored.
- **FR-009**: Revealed cells MUST persist on the device across app restarts (server persistence is
  a later feature).
- **FR-010**: The HUD MUST show Rep, rank and % of London explored, updating when fog clears.
- **FR-011**: A bottom tab bar MUST provide Map, Missions, Crew and Profile; non-Map tabs MAY show
  "coming soon" placeholders tonight.
- **FR-012**: A hidden demo control (keyboard shortcut on laptops) MUST allow revealing fog along a
  path or at a point without live GPS.
- **FR-013**: Sign-in MUST accept only @uwo.ca accounts and refuse others with a clear message.
- **FR-014**: Signed-in users MUST be able to see their identity on Profile and sign out.
- **FR-015**: The database schema MUST cover every table in the brief's data model, keep location
  history time-partitioned, and provide a per-user explored-cell count summary.
- **FR-016**: A repeatable seed MUST load the 6 verified landmark missions (with category, brief,
  year, source link), 10–15 starter missions and the 6 starter badges.
- **FR-017**: Any feature whose configuration is missing (map token, login, database) MUST hide or
  show an unavailable state without breaking the rest of the app.
- **FR-018**: No Rockstar/GTA names, logos or art may appear anywhere in the app.

### Key Entities

- **Player**: a Western student; identity, faculty, Rep, rank.
- **Revealed cell**: a ~65 m hex area a player has cleared; first and last visit times.
- **Location ping**: a timestamped position fix with accuracy; source for reveal and replay.
- **Neighbourhood / district**: a named area of London or campus zone made of cells.
- **Mission**: a task at a place (photo, check-in, bus, heist), with reward and criteria;
  landmark missions add category, brief, year and source link.
- **Badge**: a named achievement with a code and description.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: On campus Wi-Fi the map is usable within 3 seconds of opening the app.
- **SC-002**: Panning, zooming and tilting show no visible stutter on an iPhone or in the laptop frame.
- **SC-003**: The zoom from city view into campus 3D and back completes smoothly in under 1.5 seconds each way.
- **SC-004**: 100% of non-@uwo.ca sign-in attempts are refused; a @uwo.ca sign-in round trip from the home-screen app completes in under 30 seconds.
- **SC-005**: A simulated walk across campus visibly clears fog and increases % explored within 1 second of each new position.
- **SC-006**: Layout has no clipped or overlapping UI at 375 pt and 440 pt widths and in the laptop frame.
- **SC-007**: The database can be created and seeded from scratch in under 2 minutes with one command each.

## Assumptions

- The London city boundary is approximated by a simplified polygon stored in the app; precise
  municipal boundary data can replace it later.
- Before sign-in and server persistence exist, revealed cells are stored only on the device.
- The default reveal for a new device is a small area at the centre of Western campus so the demo
  never opens to a fully black screen.
- Lighting presets switch by fixed London-time windows tonight; sunset-accurate timing is an
  extended feature.
- The @uwo.ca restriction is enforced in the login provider (rule/action) and re-checked by the app.
- Database is Tiger Data (Postgres + TimescaleDB); the builder supplies the connection string.
- Non-Map tabs are placeholders tonight; missions, friends and replay arrive in later features.

# Feature Specification: Friday-Night Foundation

**Feature Branch**: `main` (solo hackathon; no feature branch)

**Created**: 2026-11-20

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "Friday-night foundation for Mustang City, per docs/product-brief.md. Installable iPhone PWA shell with phone frame on laptops; full-screen sunset-styled 3D map of London (Forest State) with branded loading; 2D/45° city view easing to detailed 3D over Western campus (Mustang City); first pass of the black fog with local/demo reveal; @uwo.ca-only login; database schema and seed with verified landmark missions; app shell with top HUD and bottom tab bar. Degrade gracefully when configuration is missing. Out of scope: photo verification, friends, replay, extended features."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Open the app and see Forest State under fog (Priority: P1)

A Western student adds Mustang City to their iPhone home screen and opens it. A branded loading
screen shows until the map is fully drawn, then a full-screen, tilted, sunset-lit map of London
appears. Every area they haven't explored is covered in black fog; a cleared patch around
their location (or a demo starting area) shows the city beneath. A top HUD shows Rep, rank and
% explored; a bottom tab bar offers Map, Missions, Crew and Profile.

**Why this priority**: This is the product's one image ("black fog clearing as you walk") and
the first thing judges see. Everything else builds on it.

**Independent Test**: Open the deployed URL on an iPhone home-screen icon and on a laptop;
confirm the loader, the fogged 3D sunset map, the HUD and the tab bar appear, and that a demo
reveal clears fog and raises % explored.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the app is opened from the home-screen icon, **When** it launches, **Then** it fills
   the screen edge to edge (no browser chrome), with HUD and tab bar clear of the notch and home bar.
2. **Given** the app is opened on a laptop browser wider than 768 px, **When** it loads, **Then** the
   identical phone layout is shown in a centered phone-shaped frame on a sunset backdrop.
3. **Given** the map is still loading, **When** the user waits, **Then** only the branded loading
   screen is visible — never a half-drawn map.
4. **Given** the map has loaded, **When** the user looks at it, **Then** it is tilted (~45°), uses
   the sunset palette with lighting matching London's current time of day, shows a horizon glow,
   shows no point-of-interest or transit clutter, and has no default map controls.
5. **Given** the user has explored nothing, **When** the map loads, **Then** all of London is
   covered in solid black fog except the revealed area, with soft edges.
6. **Given** location permission is granted (or the demo reveal is triggered), **When** a new
   position is received, **Then** fog clears around it and % explored in the HUD increases.

---

### User Story 2 - Zoom into Mustang City in 3D (Priority: P1)

From the city view the student zooms toward Western's campus. Once close enough over campus,
the camera smoothly tilts further into a detailed 3D view where campus buildings are highlighted
and mission buildings (e.g. Middlesex College) glow. Zooming back out eases back to the city view.

**Why this priority**: The brief names this the main wow moment of the demo and says to build
it first.

**Independent Test**: On the deployed app, pinch/scroll into campus and back out; confirm the
eased tilt change, highlighted buildings, and return to the city view, with no jumps.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the city view, **When** the user zooms past street level inside the campus area,
   **Then** the camera eases to ~60° pitch and campus buildings appear highlighted in 3D.
2. **Given** the campus 3D view, **When** the user zooms out or pans away from campus, **Then** the
   camera eases back to the ~45° city pitch.
3. **Given** any camera change, **When** it happens, **Then** it is animated (no instant jump).

---

### User Story 3 - Sign in with a Western account (Priority: P2)

The student taps Profile and signs in. Only @uwo.ca accounts are accepted; anyone else is
refused with a clear message. Once signed in, the profile tab shows their name and email, and
they can sign out.

**Why this priority**: Required for profiles, friends and missions tomorrow, and for the Auth0
track, but the map demo works without it.

**Independent Test**: Sign in with a @uwo.ca account from the home-screen app and see the profile;
attempt a non-@uwo.ca account and see it refused.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a signed-out user, **When** they tap Sign in and use a @uwo.ca account, **Then** they
   return to the app signed in and the Profile tab shows their identity.
2. **Given** a non-@uwo.ca account, **When** they try to sign in, **Then** access is denied with an
   explanation that only Western accounts are allowed.
3. **Given** a signed-in user, **When** they sign out, **Then** they return to the signed-out state.
4. **Given** login is not configured in an environment, **When** the user opens Profile, **Then** the
   app shows a "sign-in unavailable" state and the map keeps working.

---

### User Story 4 - Game data foundation (Priority: P2)

The builder can create the full game database (users, location history, revealed areas,
neighbourhoods, missions, completions, heists, friendships, crews, tags, collectibles, badges,
votes, rides, district control) with one command and seed it with the verified landmark missions,
starter missions and badges, so missions and progression can be built tomorrow.

**Why this priority**: Unblocks Saturday's mission and progression work; not visible in tonight's demo.

**Independent Test**: Run the schema and seed commands against an empty database; confirm all
tables exist, location history is time-partitioned, per-user explored counts can be queried, and
the seeded missions and badges are present. Re-running the seed does not duplicate rows.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an empty database, **When** the schema command runs, **Then** every table in the brief's
   data model exists with its keys and constraints.
2. **Given** the schema exists, **When** the seed runs twice, **Then** the 6 verified landmark
   missions, 10–15 starter missions and 6 starter badges exist exactly once.

---

### Edge Cases

- Location permission denied or unavailable (laptop, indoors): the map still loads; fog shows the
  default campus reveal; demo controls can reveal areas.
- Location fixes with poor accuracy (> ~50 m) or implying impossible speed are ignored.
- Map token missing: the app shows a branded "map unavailable" state instead of crashing.
- Slow network: the loader stays until the map is ready; a long wait shows a retry hint.
- Laptop window resized: the phone frame rescales and the map redraws to fit without distortion.
- User has reduced-motion enabled: camera and UI transitions are shortened.
- Position outside London: no fog is cleared (only cells inside the city count).

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: App MUST be installable to the iPhone home screen and launch full screen in portrait
  with the sunset theme and a branded icon.
- **FR-002**: On screens wider than 768 px the app MUST render the same layout inside a centered
  phone frame (~430×932 aspect), scaled to fit the window height.
- **FR-003**: App MUST show a branded loading screen until the map has finished its first full draw.
- **FR-004**: The map MUST show London in 3D at ~45° pitch with the sunset palette, horizon glow,
  lighting by London local time (day / dusk / night), and with POI labels, transit labels and
  default controls hidden. District names remain visible.
- **FR-005**: When zoomed past street level within the Western campus area, the camera MUST ease
  to ~60° pitch with campus buildings highlighted and mission buildings emphasised; leaving that
  zoom or area MUST ease back to ~45°.
- **FR-006**: All camera changes MUST be animated.
- **FR-007**: Unexplored parts of London MUST be covered in solid black fog; explored areas
  (~65 m hex cells) MUST be clear with a soft edge.
- **FR-008**: While the app is open and permission is granted, each accepted location fix MUST
  reveal the current cell and its immediate neighbours; fixes worse than ~50 m accuracy or
  implying impossible speed MUST be ignored.
- **FR-009**: Revealed cells MUST persist on the device across app restarts (server persistence is
  a later feature).
- **FR-010**: The HUD MUST show Rep, rank and % of London explored, updating when fog clears.
- **FR-011**: A bottom tab bar MUST provide Map, Missions, Crew and Profile; non-Map tabs MAY show
  "coming soon" placeholders tonight.
- **FR-012**: A hidden demo control (keyboard shortcut on laptops) MUST allow revealing fog along a
  path or at a point without live GPS.
- **FR-013**: Sign-in MUST accept only @uwo.ca accounts and refuse others with a clear message.
- **FR-014**: Signed-in users MUST be able to see their identity on Profile and sign out.
- **FR-015**: The database schema MUST cover every table in the brief's data model, keep location
  history time-partitioned, and provide a per-user explored-cell count summary.
- **FR-016**: A repeatable seed MUST load the 6 verified landmark missions (with category, brief,
  year, source link), 10–15 starter missions and the 6 starter badges.
- **FR-017**: Any feature whose configuration is missing (map token, login, database) MUST hide or
  show an unavailable state without breaking the rest of the app.
- **FR-018**: No Rockstar/GTA names, logos or art may appear anywhere in the app.

### Key Entities

- **Player**: a Western student; identity, faculty, Rep, rank.
- **Revealed cell**: a ~65 m hex area a player has cleared; first and last visit times.
- **Location ping**: a timestamped position fix with accuracy; source for reveal and replay.
- **Neighbourhood / district**: a named area of London or campus zone made of cells.
- **Mission**: a task at a place (photo, check-in, bus, heist), with reward and criteria;
  landmark missions add category, brief, year and source link.
- **Badge**: a named achievement with a code and description.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: On campus Wi-Fi the map is usable within 3 seconds of opening the app.
- **SC-002**: Panning, zooming and tilting show no visible stutter on an iPhone or in the laptop frame.
- **SC-003**: The zoom from city view into campus 3D and back completes smoothly in under 1.5 seconds each way.
- **SC-004**: 100% of non-@uwo.ca sign-in attempts are refused; a @uwo.ca sign-in round trip from the home-screen app completes in under 30 seconds.
- **SC-005**: A simulated walk across campus visibly clears fog and increases % explored within 1 second of each new position.
- **SC-006**: Layout has no clipped or overlapping UI at 375 pt and 440 pt widths and in the laptop frame.
- **SC-007**: The database can be created and seeded from scratch in under 2 minutes with one command each.

## Assumptions

- The London city boundary is approximated by a simplified polygon stored in the app; precise
  municipal boundary data can replace it later.
- Before sign-in and server persistence exist, revealed cells are stored only on the device.
- The default reveal for a new device is a small area at the centre of Western campus so the demo
  never opens to a fully black screen.
- Lighting presets switch by fixed London-time windows tonight; sunset-accurate timing is an
  extended feature.
- The @uwo.ca restriction is enforced in the login provider (rule/action) and re-checked by the app.
- Database is Tiger Data (Postgres + TimescaleDB); the builder supplies the connection string.
- Non-Map tabs are placeholders tonight; missions, friends and replay arrive in later features.

# Implementation Plan: Friday-Night Foundation

**Branch**: `main` (spec dir `001-friday-foundation`) | **Date**: 2026-11-20 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `specs/001-friday-foundation/spec.md`

## Summary

Turn the existing PWA shell into the real game screen: a single persistent Mapbox Standard map of
London styled into the sunset look, a branded loader, an eased 45°→60° camera mode switch over
Western's campus with neon campus-building extrusions, a first-pass black fog (one GeoJSON polygon
with H3 res-10 holes, device-persisted), a HUD + tab bar + bottom sheet, hidden demo controls,
Auth0 v4 login gated to @uwo.ca, and a Tiger Data schema + idempotent seed. Every integration
degrades gracefully when its env vars are absent.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5, Node 24 (local), Node 22+ on Vercel

**Primary Dependencies**: Next.js 16.4 (App Router, `cacheComponents: true`), React 19.3,
Tailwind v4, motion 14, mapbox-gl 3.35 (Standard style), h3-js 4.5, @auth0/nextjs-auth0 4.x,
postgres (porsager) 3.x

**Storage**: Tiger Data (Postgres + TimescaleDB); device `localStorage` for revealed cells tonight

**Testing**: `npm run build` + `npm run lint`; browser checks in the built-in browser /
Playwright WebKit iPhone profile; manual iPhone home-screen check (Principle VII)

**Target Platform**: iOS Safari 17+ standalone PWA; desktop Chromium/Safari in phone frame

**Project Type**: Single Next.js web app (UI + API routes in one project)

**Performance Goals**: 60 fps map interaction; map usable < 3 s; fog rebuild < 16 ms for ≤ 5k cells

**Constraints**: one map instance; no DOM markers; no `position: fixed`/`100vh` inside the app;
secrets server-only; works with zero env vars (map shows "unavailable" state)

**Scale/Scope**: ~100 hackathon users; London boundary ≈ 30k res-10 cells

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

| Principle | Check | Status |
|---|---|---|
| I. Phone-First PWA | All new UI lives in `.app-root`, absolute-positioned, uses `--safe-*` vars; pointer events; demo panel is the only element outside the frame (by design, laptop-only) | ✅ |
| II. Original IP Only | Names Forest State / Mustang City; original icon; no GTA assets | ✅ |
| III. Secrets Server-Side | Auth0 + DATABASE_URL used only in `lib/auth0.ts`, `proxy.ts`, `scripts/db.mjs`; client gets only `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN` | ✅ |
| IV. Core Six Always Work | Fog + 3D zoom built tonight; missing env → hidden/unavailable, never crash | ✅ |
| V. Demo Reliability & Perf | Map in ref, created once; fog single polygon via `setData`; symbol/circle layers only; DPR capped at 2; loader until `idle`; demo walk control | ✅ |
| VI. Ship Continuously | build + lint before push; Vercel from `main` | ✅ |
| VII. Simple Over Clever | Module-level stores + `useSyncExternalStore`; no state library; no test framework | ✅ |

Post-design re-check: ✅ no violations; Complexity Tracking empty.

## Project Structure

### Documentation (this feature)

```text
specs/001-friday-foundation/
├── plan.md
├── research.md
├── data-model.md
├── quickstart.md
├── contracts/
│   ├── http-routes.md
│   ├── demo-controls.md
│   └── db-scripts.md
└── tasks.md            # /speckit-tasks
```

### Source Code (repository root)

```text
app/
├── layout.tsx            # shell + phone frame (exists)
├── page.tsx              # GameScreen
├── globals.css           # tokens, shell, mapbox attribution styling
├── manifest.ts, icon*.tsx, apple-icon.tsx (exist)
components/
├── GameScreen.tsx        # client: map + HUD + tabs + sheet + demo panel
├── map/MapView.tsx       # creates the single Mapbox map, wires layers + camera
├── map/LoadingScreen.tsx
├── Hud.tsx
├── TabBar.tsx
├── Sheet.tsx             # bottom sheet for non-map tabs
├── ProfilePanel.tsx      # auth state
├── LocationPrompt.tsx
└── DemoPanel.tsx         # press D
lib/
├── geo.ts                # London boundary, campus bbox/polygon, mission building polygons, demo walk
├── fog.ts                # revealed-cell store, H3 reveal, fog GeoJSON builder, % explored
├── location.ts           # watchPosition with accuracy/speed filtering
├── mapStyle.ts           # Standard config, London-clock light preset, atmosphere, layer ids
├── auth0.ts              # Auth0Client or null
└── brandIcon.tsx (exists)
proxy.ts                  # Auth0 middleware (no-op when unconfigured)
db/
├── schema.sql
└── seed.sql
scripts/db.mjs            # `npm run db:schema` / `npm run db:seed`
auth0/uwo-only-action.js  # paste into Auth0 Actions → Login flow
```

**Structure Decision**: single Next.js project at repo root, matching the brief's suggested layout.

## Complexity Tracking

No violations.

# Research: Friday-Night Foundation

## R1. Base map styling on Mapbox Standard
- **Decision**: `style: mapbox://styles/mapbox/standard` with `config.basemap` set at creation:
  `lightPreset` from London clock, `showPointOfInterestLabels/showTransitLabels/showPedestrianRoads:
  false`, colour overrides (water → purple, motorways → pink, trunks → orange). Atmosphere via
  `map.setFog()` with pink/orange horizon and night-purple space colour.
- **Rationale**: Standard already ships lit 3D buildings, trees and landmarks; config keeps one style.
- **Alternatives**: custom Studio style (slower to iterate, needs account work); LUT theme
  (deferred to polish — needs an authored LUT image).

## R2. Campus 3D highlight
- **Decision**: add a `mapbox-streets-v8` vector source and a `fill-extrusion` layer on the
  `building` source-layer, filtered with `within` the campus polygon, neon gradient colours,
  `fill-extrusion-emissive-strength` so it glows under night lighting, opacity fading in z15→15.5.
  A second layer filtered `within` mission-building polygons (Middlesex College) glows gold.
- **Rationale**: deterministic, no reliance on feature ids or featureset APIs.
- **Alternatives**: Standard `buildings` featureset + feature-state (needs stable ids per building).

## R3. Camera mode switch
- **Decision**: on `moveend`, compute mode = `campus` if `zoom ≥ 15` and centre inside campus bbox,
  else `city`. On mode change only, `easeTo({ pitch: 60 | 45, duration: 900 })`. User-driven pitch
  inside a mode is left alone. Reduced motion → duration 0.
- **Rationale**: avoids fighting the user's gestures and avoids re-entrant `moveend` loops.

## R4. Fog geometry
- **Decision**: one `FeatureCollection` with a MultiPolygon: polygon 1 = London boundary outer ring
  with each revealed region's outer loop as a hole; plus each revealed region's inner loops (unrevealed
  islands) as extra fog polygons. Built from `cellsToMultiPolygon(cells, true)`. Soft edge = black
  line layer with `line-blur` along revealed outer loops. Fog rebuild debounced 150 ms.
- **Rationale**: Principle V; one feature regardless of reveal count.
- **Alternatives**: one feature per hex (thousands of features, grid look).

## R5. % explored
- **Decision**: denominator = `polygonToCells(LONDON_BOUNDARY, 10).length`, computed once lazily
  (≈30k cells, ~50 ms) and used as a Set to reject reveals outside London.
- **Rationale**: exact under the same grid used for reveal.

## R6. Location filtering
- **Decision**: `watchPosition({ enableHighAccuracy: true, maximumAge: 2000 })`; drop fixes with
  `accuracy > 50` m or implied speed > 45 m/s vs last accepted fix. Started only after the user taps
  the location prompt (iOS permission etiquette). Fixes go to the fog store and the player-dot source,
  never React state.

## R7. Auth0 v4 on Next 16
- **Decision**: `lib/auth0.ts` exports `Auth0Client | null` (null when any of `AUTH0_DOMAIN`,
  `AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AUTH0_SECRET` is missing). `proxy.ts` calls
  `auth0.middleware()` or passes through. `onCallback` re-checks email domain and sends non-@uwo.ca
  sessions to `/auth/logout?returnTo=/?denied=uwo`. The primary gate is an Auth0 Login Action
  (`auth0/uwo-only-action.js`). Client reads `/auth/profile` (200 user / 401|204 signed out /
  other = unavailable) — no provider needed, layout stays static under `cacheComponents`.
- **Alternatives**: `getSession()` in layout (forces dynamic rendering + Suspense).

## R8. Database access
- **Decision**: plain SQL files run by `scripts/db.mjs` using `postgres` (porsager); seed uses
  `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on natural keys (`missions.slug`, `badges.code`).
- **Continuous aggregate**: `user_daily_cells` over `location_pings` grouped by

# Quickstart: validate the Friday-night foundation

## Prereqs
- `.env.local` from `.env.example` with at least `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN`.
- Optional: Auth0 app (callback `<base>/auth/callback`, logout `<base>`, `<base>/?denied=uwo`) with
  `auth0/uwo-only-action.js` added to the Login flow; Tiger Data `DATABASE_URL`.

## Scenarios
1. **Zero config**: unset all env vars, `npm run build && npm start` → app loads, map area shows
   "Map unavailable" card, tabs work, Profile says sign-in unavailable. (FR-017)
2. **Map + loader**: with token, open `/` → branded loader, then tilted sunset map with black fog
   and a clear patch on campus; no POI/transit labels; no default controls. (US1)
3. **3D zoom**: scroll into campus past z15 → eases to ~60°, neon campus buildings, Middlesex glows;
   zoom out → back to ~45°. (US2)
4. **Fog reveal**: press D → Walk campus → fog clears along the path, HUD % rises; reload → still
   cleared. (FR-007–FR-012)
5. **Phone frame**: window > 768 px shows framed phone; < 768 px fills the viewport; resize keeps map
   undistorted. (FR-002)
6. **Auth**: Profile → Sign in with @uwo.ca → identity shown; non-@uwo.ca → refused message. (US3)
7. **DB**: `npm run db:schema && npm run db:seed` twice → no errors, seed counts unchanged. (US4)
8. **Gates**: `npm run lint && npm run build` pass.

-- Mustang City schema (Tiger Data: Postgres + TimescaleDB). Idempotent: safe to re-run.
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;

DO $$ BEGIN
  CREATE TYPE mission_type AS ENUM ('photo', 'checkin', 'bus', 'heist');
EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL; END $$;
DO $$ BEGIN
  CREATE TYPE mission_category AS ENUM ('history', 'film_tv', 'viral');
EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL; END $$;
DO $$ BEGIN
  CREATE TYPE friendship_status AS ENUM ('pending', 'accepted');
EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL; END $$;
DO $$ BEGIN
  CREATE TYPE heist_status AS ENUM ('open', 'complete', 'expired');
EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL; END $$;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id            uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  auth0_id      text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  email         text NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (lower(email) LIKE '%@uwo.ca'),
  display_name  text NOT NULL,
  faculty       text,
  rep           integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (rep >= 0),
  rank          text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Frosh',
  created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Only hypertable: raw GPS fixes. Feeds reveal, replay and Wrapped.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS location_pings (
  user_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  ts          timestamptz NOT NULL,
  lat         double precision NOT NULL,
  lng         double precision NOT NULL,
  accuracy_m  real,
  h3_cell     text NOT NULL
);
SELECT create_hypertable('location_pings', by_range('ts', INTERVAL '1 day'), if_not_exists => TRUE);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS location_pings_user_ts ON location_pings (user_id, ts DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS revealed_cells (
  user_id          uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  h3_cell          text NOT NULL,
  first_seen_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  last_visited_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, h3_cell)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS neighbourhoods (
  id        serial PRIMARY KEY,
  name      text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  polygon   jsonb NOT NULL,          -- GeoJSON Polygon
  h3_cells  text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS missions (
  id           serial PRIMARY KEY,
  slug         text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  title        text NOT NULL,
  briefing     text NOT NULL,
  type         mission_type NOT NULL,
  lat          double precision NOT NULL,
  lng          double precision NOT NULL,
  radius_m     integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 75 CHECK (radius_m > 0),
  criteria     text NOT NULL,        -- plain-language check sent to Gemini
  rep_reward   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 100 CHECK (rep_reward >= 0),
  creator_id   uuid REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  is_official  boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  active       boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  -- landmark missions
  category     mission_category,
  brief        text,
  year         integer,
  source_url   text
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mission_completions (
  id             serial PRIMARY KEY,
  mission_id     integer NOT NULL REFERENCES missions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id        uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  photo_url      text,
  lat            double precision,
  lng            double precision,
  gemini_pass    boolean,
  gemini_reason  text,
  completed_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (mission_id, user_id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS mission_completions_user ON mission_completions (user_id, completed_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS heist_attempts (
  id          serial PRIMARY KEY,
  mission_id  integer NOT NULL REFERENCES missions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  started_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  member_ids  uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  photo_url   text,
  status      heist_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open'
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS friendships (
  user_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  friend_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  status      friendship_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, friend_id),
  CHECK (user_id <> friend_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crews (
  id          serial PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  member_ids  uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tags (
  id          serial PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  h3_cell     text NOT NULL,
  lat         double precision NOT NULL,
  lng         double precision NOT NULL,
  note        text,
  photo_url   text,
  votes       integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tags_h3_cell ON tags (h3_cell);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collectibles (
  id         serial PRIMARY KEY,
  name       text NOT NULL,
  lat        double precision NOT NULL,
  lng        double precision NOT NULL,
  lore_text  text
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collectible_finds (
  user_id         uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  collectible_id  integer NOT NULL REFERENCES collectibles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  found_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, collectible_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS badges (
  id           serial PRIMARY KEY,
  code         text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name         text NOT NULL,
  description  text NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_badges (
  user_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  badge_id   integer NOT NULL REFERENCES badges(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  earned_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, badge_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mission_votes (
  mission_id  integer NOT NULL REFERENCES missions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  value       smallint NOT NULL CHECK (value IN (-1, 1)),
  PRIMARY KEY (mission_id, user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rides (
  id          serial PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  route_id    text NOT NULL,
  start_stop  text,
  end_stop    text,
  started_at  timestamptz NOT NULL,
  ended_at    timestamptz
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS district_control (
  neighbourhood_id  integer PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES neighbourhoods(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  faculty           text NOT NULL,
  rep_total         integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS user_daily_cells
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '1 day', ts) AS bucket,
       user_id,
       h3_cell,
       count(*) AS pings
FROM location_pings
GROUP BY bucket, user_id, h3_cell
WITH NO DATA;

SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('user_daily_cells',
  start_offset => INTERVAL '30 days',
  end_offset => INTERVAL '1 minute',
  schedule_interval => INTERVAL '15 minutes',
  if_not_exists => TRUE);

# Mustang City

GTA 6-inspired fog-of-war exploration PWA for Western students (Hack Western 13, solo build).
The full product brief is in [docs/product-brief.md](docs/product-brief.md) — read it before planning features.

## Ground rules
- Mobile-first PWA for iPhone home-screen use. On wide screens the same app renders inside a centered phone frame (`components/PhoneFrame.tsx`) — never a separate desktop layout.
- Inside the app, size UI to the app container (`position: absolute`), never `position: fixed` or `100vh`. Only the outer shell uses `100dvh`.
- Never use Rockstar/GTA names, logos, art or music. London = "Forest State", Western campus = "Mustang City".
- All API keys stay server-side (Vercel env vars). The browser only gets `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN`.
- Core six features (fog map, 3D campus zoom, photo missions, login/profiles, friends, replay) must keep working; extended features must not break them.
- Build order and cut list are in the brief's "Build plan" section.

## Stack
Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind v4, Motion, Mapbox GL JS (Standard style), h3-js, Auth0, Tiger Data (Postgres/TimescaleDB), Gemini API, Vercel.

## Workflow
- Planning: Spec Kit (`/speckit-constitution` → `/speckit-specify` → `/speckit-plan` → `/speckit-tasks` → `/speckit-implement`).
- Design: `/impeccable`, frontend-design, web-design-guidelines skills.
- Testing: Playwright MCP (WebKit, iPhone 15) for layout; agent-browser for faked-GPS walks.
- Entire is enabled — session checkpoints are pushed with the repo.
- `npm run build` must pass before every push; Vercel deploys from `main`.

# Mustang City

**Graduate knowing your city.** A GTA 6-inspired mobile web app (PWA) that turns London, Ontario into *Forest State* — a map covered in black fog that clears only where you've physically been. Built solo at Hack Western 13.

See [docs/product-brief.md](docs/product-brief.md) for the full brief.

## Develop

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local   # fill in keys
npm run dev
```

1. Import `RyanPeters06/mustang-city` at vercel.com/new (framework: Next.js, defaults are fine).
2. Add the env vars from `.env.example` in Project → Settings → Environment Variables.
3. Every push to `main` deploys. Add the custom domain (mustangcity.club) under Settings → Domains.

## Install on iPhone

Open the deployed URL in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen → launch from the icon.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\peter\hack-western\.claude\skills\impeccable

This skill gives you the tools and permission to make design that earns the name out-of-distribution craft. Work as an award-winning design director would: production-grade code, a clear POV, a deep grasp of what the client and its users need, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Finish the job. No hedging, no shortcuts: the deliverable is complete, except assets the user must provide.
- Scale ambition to the surface's mode (see Modes). Persuade and Experience get full commitment: bold, distinct work with a point of view. On Operate and Read, ambition shows as precision and restraint, and patterns the visitor already knows earn their place.
- Verify by looking at the rendered result at the sizes it ships at (web: `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable shot <page>`), and batch the checks: fix what one look shows before looking again.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md (long ones as a map: read the sections your task needs), the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface, a replacement visual world, or a build from an approved comp. Some playbooks come in parts; read the part this request needs in the same step: [reference/new-work-world.md](reference/new-work-world.md) when a visual world is created or replaced (a redesign, a new look, or no established world), [reference/new-work-comp.md](reference/new-work-comp.md) for a build from an approved comp or on a comp-led build path, and [reference/critique-rubric.md](reference/critique-rubric.md) for a critique whose Assessment A runs in this context (a native platform, or no sub-agent tool); a delegated Assessment A gets the rubric's path in its prompt instead. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

**Launcher unavailable:** On the first refusal or failure, don’t retry; send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, including reading [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Loaded symbols stay out of the decoration.** A subject's world does not license emblems tied to militarism, supremacy, or hate movements as motifs, badges, or ornament, such as the Rising Sun flag's rays, the Confederate battle flag, or Nazi-era insignia and their stylised variants; reach for that world's neutral forms instead. Content that documents such a symbol as fact stays as it is.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.

## Commands

| Command | Category | Description | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `craft [feature]` | Build | Deprecated alias for an ordinary new-work request | [reference/craft.md](reference/craft.md) |
| `shape [feature]` | Build | Plan UX/UI before writing code | [reference/shape.md](reference/shape.md) |
| `init` | Build | Capture durable product context in PRODUCT.md | [reference/init.md](reference/init.md) |
| `document` | Build | Generate DESIGN.md from existing project code | [reference/document.md](reference/document.md) |
| `extract [target]` | Build | Pull reusable tokens and components into design system | [reference/extract.md](reference/extract.md) |
| `critique [target]` | Evaluate | UX design review with heuristic scoring | [reference/critique.md](reference/critique.md) |
| `audit [target]` | Evaluate | Technical quality checks (a11y, perf, responsive) | [reference/audit.md](reference/audit.md) · native: [reference/audit.native.md](reference/audit.native.md) |
| `polish [target]` | Refine | Final quality pass before shipping | [reference/polish.md](reference/polish.md) |
| `bolder [target]` | Refine | Amplify safe or bland designs | [reference/bolder.md](reference/bolder.md) |
| `quieter [target]` | Refine | Tone down aggressive or overstimulating designs | [reference/quieter.md](reference/quieter.md) |
| `distill [target]` | Refine | Strip to essence, remove complexity | [reference/distill.md](reference/distill.md) |
| `harden [target]` | Refine | Production-ready: errors, i18n, edge cases | [reference/harden.md](reference/harden.md) |
| `onboard [target]` | Refine | Design first-run flows, empty states, activation | [reference/onboard.md](reference/onboard.md) |
| `animate [target]` | Enhance | Add purposeful animations and motion | [reference/animate.md](reference/animate.md) |
| `colorize [target]` | Enhance | Add strategic color to monochromatic UIs | [reference/colorize.md](reference/colorize.md) |
| `typeset [target]` | Enhance | Improve typography hierarchy and fonts | [reference/typeset.md](reference/typeset.md) |
| `layout [target]` | Enhance | Fix spacing, rhythm, and visual hierarchy | [reference/layout.md](reference/layout.md) |
| `delight [target]` | Enhance | Add personality and memorable touches | [reference/delight.md](reference/delight.md) |
| `overdrive [target]` | Enhance | Push past conventional limits | [reference/overdrive.md](reference/overdrive.md) |
| `clarify [target]` | Fix | Improve UX copy, labels, and error messages | [reference/clarify.md](reference/clarify.md) |
| `adapt [target]` | Fix | Adapt for different devices and screen sizes | [reference/adapt.md](reference/adapt.md) · native: [reference/adapt.native.md](reference/adapt.native.md) |
| `optimize [target]` | Fix | Diagnose and fix UI performance | [reference/optimize.md](reference/optimize.md) |
| `live` | Iterate | Visual variant mode: pick elements in the browser, iterate on alternatives | [reference/live.md](reference/live.md) |
| `generate [n] [action] [element]` | Iterate | Variants, versions, or alternatives of a named element to choose from in the live browser; no manual picking | [reference/generate.md](reference/generate.md) |

Routing:

- **No argument:** read [routing.md](reference/routing.md) and present its context-aware menu; never auto-run a command.
- **Explicit or clearly implied request to run a command:** load its reference (native variant on native platforms) and follow it. Ask once if two commands fit.
- **Workflow or command-selection question:** read [Workflow questions](reference/routing.md#workflow-questions).
- **Otherwise:** treat the request as general design work. Missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work; a narrow refinement of existing code proceeds on the incumbent implementation as `impeccable context` directs, offering init afterward rather than blocking on it.
- `teach` aliases `init`. `craft` is a deprecated alias for ordinary new-work and adds nothing. `shape` owns task discovery, then enters new-work only for visual-world and surface-concept decisions.

After init writes PRODUCT.md, resume without rerunning `impeccable context`; init loads the native platform reference itself when the platform it recorded is `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive`.

**Pin / Unpin:** `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable pin <pin|unpin> <command>` creates or removes a standalone `/<command>` shortcut. Report the script's result concisely; relay stderr verbatim on error.

**Hooks:** `/impeccable hooks <on|off|status|ignore-rule|ignore-file|ignore-value|reset>` manages the design detector hook for this project (auto-runs the detector after UI file edits and surfaces findings). Load [reference/hooks.md](reference/hooks.md) when the user invokes it with any argument.

**Doctor:** `/impeccable doctor` reports and repairs drift between this project's Impeccable artifacts (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and its sidecar, config, surface briefs, the hook) and what this version reads. Load [reference/doctor.md](reference/doctor.md) when the user invokes it, or when they ask what is out of date, stale, or needs refreshing. A `CONTEXT_STALE` directive in Setup's output is the cheap subset of the same report; act on it there per its own instructions rather than running doctor unasked.

**Foundations:** `/impeccable foundations` runs `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable foundations` and walks the user through the product-foundations roadmap (secrets, 404 page, icons, CI and more); `/impeccable foundations <id>` fixes that one item. Load [reference/foundations.md](reference/foundations.md) when the user invokes it.

**Never repair drift as a side effect of a design task.** A `CONTEXT_STALE` finding is reported, not acted on, unless the user asks. The one exception is a finding marked `auto`, which the next write to that file performs anyway.

# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

## Platform

web

## Users

All Western University students, equally — not only first-years. They use Mustang City on an
iPhone, launched from the home-screen icon, mostly outdoors: walking across campus, through London
neighbourhoods, or riding LTC buses, often in bright sunlight and one-handed. Secondary audiences:
friend groups (crews), faculties competing for districts, and hackathon judges watching the same
phone screen in a laptop phone frame.

## Product Purpose

Students stay in a small loop (campus, Richmond Row, one or two bus routes) for four years.
Mustang City turns London, Ontario into "Forest State", a map covered in black fog that clears only
where the student has physically been, and gives them reasons, routes and company to leave the
bubble: AI-verified photo missions, bus rides, hidden collectibles and co-op heists. Success is
% of London explored, neighbourhoods unlocked, missions completed, and heists done with people the
student didn't already know. Tagline: "Graduate knowing your city."

## Positioning

Exploration trackers only record where you've been. Mustang City is built for Western: the fog is
the game board, and missions verified by GPS + Gemini vision, faculty turf wars, bus missions and
multi-person heists turn exploring into a social, competitive open-world game. GTA 6-inspired in
feel, entirely original in names and assets.

## Operating Context

- Installed as a PWA from Safari (Share → Add to Home Screen); no background GPS, so fog clears
  only while the app is open.
- Live demo at Hack Western 13 (Nov 20–22, 2026) runs on a laptop in a phone frame with replay mode
  and hidden demo controls (press D); the real iPhone and a recorded video are backups.
- Map is always full screen; all UI floats over it. Portrait only.

## Capabilities and Constraints

- Core six (never cut): black-fog map, 2D→3D zoom into Mustang City, photo missions with Gemini
  verification, @uwo.ca-only login and profiles, friends, replay mode.
- Extended features follow the brief's build order (time-of-day palette, goose boss, tags, AI radio,
  Wrapped, live buses, turf, heists…).
- Terminology: London = Forest State; Western campus = Mustang City; Rep (single currency); ranks
  Frosh → Local → Made → Legend of Forest State; quest-giver = The Goose; mission result moment =
  "MISSION PASSED".
- Constraints: solo 36-hour build; 60 fps map on iPhone; secrets server-side; laptop frame must be
  identical to the phone UI. Neighbourhood boundary source is undecided.

## Brand Commitments

- Name: Mustang City (product and in-game campus); Forest State (London).
- Voice: playful crime-boss. The Goose speaks like a deadpan open-world quest-giver; UI copy is
  short and cheeky, never mean.
- Never use Rockstar/GTA names (Leonida, Vice City), logos, wordmarks, screenshots, art, characters
  or music. Public copy may say "GTA 6-inspired" only.
- Binding palette from the brief: night #140A2E, fog #000000, pink #FF4F8B, orange #FF8A3D,
  gold #FFC857, purple #7B2FF7, teal #2EE6D6 (teal = you, friends, buses).

## Evidence on Hand

- Verified landmark facts with sources: `docs/product-brief.md` → Landmark missions, seeded in
  `db/seed.sql`.
- No testimonials, user counts, sponsor deals or press exist yet; sponsored missions are a pitch,
  not a fact. Viral-video spots are unseeded until each location is confirmed from a reliable source.

## Product Principles

1. The fog is the product: every screen serves uncovering the city.
2. Demo-proof: every core moment works without live GPS or a camera.
3. Real places, real facts: landmark text comes from stored, sourced facts; AI restyles, never invents.
4. Get students out together: features that create meetings (heists, crews, turf) beat solo stats.
5. Phone first, always: what the iPhone shows is what the judges see.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

Readable outdoors in direct sunlight (WCAG AA contrast minimum on all text over the map),
reduced-motion support for camera and UI animation, 44 pt tap targets, 16 px+ inputs.
Privacy by default: live location sharing off unless opted in, blurred to neighbourhood level.

content.text:
I ran all four Spec Kit steps and `/impeccable init`, and pushed everything to `main`. Lint and build pass. I haven't seen the actual map yet, because there's no Mapbox token locally, so only the "map unavailable" screen has been checked.

**Planning docs:**
- A project constitution with seven ground rules, taken from your brief.
- The spec, plan, research notes, data model, contracts, quickstart and a 25-task list in `specs/001-friday-foundation/`. All 25 tasks are done.

**What's built:**
- **Map:** one map of London (Forest State) in the sunset look. Lighting follows London's clock, labels and default controls are hidden, and a branded loading screen stays up until the map is ready.
- **3D zoom:** past street level over campus, the camera eases from 45° to 60°. Campus buildings show as neon 3D blocks and Middlesex College glows gold. Zooming out eases back.
- **Fog:** a single black polygon with explored areas cut out. It's saved on the phone, and the top bar shows % explored, Rep and rank. GPS fixes with poor accuracy or impossible speed are ignored.
- **App shell:** top bar, bottom tabs, a draggable bottom sheet, and a "turn on location" prompt.
- **Demo controls:** press D on the laptop to walk campus, fly to campus or the city, reveal fog, or reset it.
- **Login:** Auth0, limited to @uwo.ca. An Auth0 Action (`auth0/uwo-only-action.js`) blocks other emails and the app checks again.
- **Database:** every table from the brief, with GPS pings stored as a TimescaleDB hypertable and a continuous aggregate for explored cells. A seed adds the 6 landmark missions, 8 starter missions and 6 badges, and is safe to re-run.
- **PRODUCT.md:** written from `/impeccable init`, broadened to all students as you chose, with the playful crime-boss voice.

**What I checked:**
- Every part degrades cleanly when its keys are missing. Without a token you get the "map unavailable" card, without Auth0 you get "sign-in unavailable", and the tabs and sheet still work. I checked this in the laptop frame and at 375 px.
- A scripted campus walk in Node cleared 51 cells, rebuilt the fog in about 6 ms, and positions outside London were ignored.

**Not done yet:**
- **The map itself hasn't been seen.** Without a token I couldn't see the styling or the campus 3D, so the colour settings and building layers may need tweaking. The landmark coordinates are approximate, so check them before Saturday's walk.
- **The database scripts haven't been run.** That needs your `DATABASE_URL`.
- **The pixel-ratio cap is missing.** Mapbox v3 has no option for it, so if frame rate dips on the iPhone, turning off 3D trees or facades is the next step.

## Connecting mustangcity.rodeo to Vercel

**1. Vercel** (if you haven't imported the project yet):
- Go to vercel.com/new and import `RyanPeters06/mustang-city` with the default Next.js settings.
- Add `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN`, plus the Auth0 keys if you have them, then deploy.
- In the project, go to **Settings → Domains**. Add `mustangcity.rodeo`, and accept when Vercel offers to add `www.mustangcity.rodeo` as well.
- Vercel then shows the DNS records it wants. Keep that page open.

**2. Porkbun** (Domain Management, then the DNS Records link on mustangcity.rodeo):
- **Delete the 2 existing records.** They're most likely Porkbun's parking page, and they'd conflict.
- **Root record:** type **A**, Host empty, Answer = the IP Vercel shows (usually `76.76.21.21`), TTL 600.
- **www record:** type **CNAME**, Host `www`, Answer = the value Vercel shows (usually `cname.vercel-dns.com`).
- Leave the Porkbun nameservers as they are. Records are enough; you don't need to switch to Vercel's nameservers.

**3. Back in Vercel:** the domains turn green and HTTPS is issued automatically, usually within minutes. Then:
- Set `APP_BASE_URL=https://mustangcity.rodeo` in Vercel and redeploy.
- In Auth0, add `https://mustangcity.rodeo/auth/callback` as a callback URL, and `https://mustangcity.rodeo` and `https://mustangcity.rodeo/?denied=uwo` as logout URLs.
- In Mapbox, add the domain to the token's allowed URLs.

The brief's domain prize ("Best Domain Name from GoDaddy Registry") requires a GoDaddy Registry extension, and I'm not sure .rodeo is one. Check with MLH before you list that prize on Devpost.

The Porkbun page you pasted includes your home address and phone number as the registrant contact. Contact Privacy is on, so the public lookup hides them, but avoid pasting that page anywhere public.

content.text:
I created [.env.local](.env.local) from the example file. Git ignores it, so whatever you put in it stays on your machine.

1. Get a token at **account.mapbox.com → Tokens**. Your **Default public token** (it starts with `pk.`) works, or you can create a new public one. Don't use a secret `sk.` token, because this one is visible in the browser.
2. Paste it after `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN=` in `.env.local` and save.
3. Optional: under the token's URL restrictions, add `http://localhost:3000` and `https://mustangcity.rodeo`. If you restrict it and leave localhost out, the local map won't load.
4. Add the same variable in **Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables** so the deployed site gets the map too.

Tell me when it's saved. Then I'll start the dev server, check the sunset styling, the fog, the campus 3D zoom and the demo walk, and fix whatever looks off.
